subject: Optimization of binomial model with 4 million data (new to INLA)

messages.author: 80f8c8f7118c2f36
messages.subject: Optimization of binomial model with 4 million data (new to INLA)
parts:
Dear group, 
I'm totally new to INLA and I'm trying to run a binomial model with a large dataset of 4 million data. I got some help from a colleague to start with but still I'm a bit confused.
I'm investigating if the condition of an animal ("atrisk" is my response variable and gets "0" is the animal is in a safe area, and "1" if it is at a risky area) is dependent on a series of explanatory variables. I expect linear effects for some of them, and non-linear effects for two of them (included as rw2). I have many individuals measured that I need to include as random factors, and also strong temporal autocorrelation within each animal.
After reading some thread on the group I have tried the model below, in which all variables are scaled. I have defined the "diagonals" for the "rw2" terms as suggested in some other threads, and also the argument control.inla that you see  below.

inla_bin<- inla(atrisk ~ 1 + Lcm + distance_to_border+ areahr + PPscore+
                  f(week, model="rw2",cyclic=TRUE, diagonal=1e-4)+
                  f(hour,model="rw2",cyclic=TRUE,diagonal=1e-4)+
                  f(tag_id_inla,model="iid")+
                  f(TimeStep.coa,model="ar1", replicate=as.numeric(tag_id_inla)),
                data=scaled_subsetCOAs,
                family="binomial",verbose=TRUE, num.threads=24,control.inla = list(cmin = 0 ))

I have some pretty basic questions and sorry if they are too basic:

1- I have tried the model with a subset of data (80,000 data) and it took 4 hours in a remote server with the following characteristics:

Brand: Dell Inc.
Model: Precision 7920 Tower
Processor: Intel(R) Xeon(R) Gold 6130 CPU @ 2.10GHz
Architecture: x86_64
Cores: 16

Memory:

              total        used        free      shared  buff/cache   available
Memory:         92G        685M         89G         26M        2,9G         91G
Swap:            0B          0B          0B

Is there any argument/methods that I can pass to INLA to improve the computation time?

2- I expect that both "hour" and "week" have a non-linear cyclic effect so this is why I intuitively set the cyclic argument to TRUE. Those two variables range between 0-23 and 1-52 in the real world but they were scaled before the model (perhaps not necessary?). Have I correctly specified that I want/expect a cyclic pattern or is there any other argument needed? Comparing with the gam world, what I'm trying to do is the equivalent to s(hour, bs="cc")...

3- I left the model running overnight in the remote server and this morning the VERBOSE was not moving and the last message was the following. Is that and error or was it running ok? (I stopped the process anyway):

file: smtp-taucs.c  hgid: b84cb08f11c9  date: Thu Jul 12 13:38:25 2018 +0300
        Function: GMRFLib_build_sparse_matrix_TAUCS(), Line: 751, Thread: 0

4- The random factor (the animal ID, here coded as "tag_id_inla") has been entered, in a preliminary model, as a factor being each level the ID code of the animal (e.g. "fish-3432-01") ; however I was suggested to rename factor levels so that they go from 1 to the maximum number of levels (here 1 to 319)...is this strictly necessary?

I appreciate before hand any advise you could provide.

Best,

David

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Optimization of binomial model with 4 million data (new to INLA)
parts:
The option is to use the pardiso library; see

inla.pardiso()

and follow the guidelines.

you'll need an academic email to get a free license.

H

parts:
I would think the
+ f(TimeStep.coa,model="ar1", replicate=as.numeric(tag_id_inla))
in the formula makes the model slow.

You can test, just to test, what happens if you remove the replicate=...

Can you do: max(TimeStep.coa) and max(tag_id_inla)? Probably, the internal inla representation has as size the product of these numbers. The 80k of your data may not be the relevant number, if the product of these numbers are bigger than 80k.

Best,
Haakon

parts:
IMHO you should also provide custom priors. 'Small' values (range 5 -10) can result in huge effects in combination with a logit link. https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/oik.05985 is a nice paper about this. Note that the paper is based on STAN, so only the first 6 pages are useful for INLA users.

Consider `rw1` instead of the `ar1`. It can model the same complexity with a single hyperparameter.

And check your data for quasicomplete separation.

Best regards,

messages.author: 9940b4fcc153c7d7
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Re: Optimization of binomial model with 4 million data (new to INLA)
parts:
For your question: Yes, this is why I said "just to test". The point is not to look at the results, but at the computational time.

I would suggest strong shrinkage priors in any case! Binomial data can "run away" sometimes.

If you save your logfile (with verbose=T), we can take a quick look and see if the convergence is bad.

Some times, people code the group-thing not from 1 to 49 but from 1901 to 1949, so INLA believes it must represent 1949 replicates.

Haakon
